title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 'deuxième mouture' of Analysis situs (June 1986), Grothendieck is axiomatizing 'ateliers'. These are categories or posets of 'figures' with a sub-figure relation ≪, a boundary operator ∂ and a class L of minimal ('linear', point-like) elements. Fig(L) denotes the atelier of all figures built on L, and M is a distinguished class of figures (admissible or 'model' figures). The surrounding pages check which axioms At n, and the set-theoretic variants 'At ens n', hold automatically in particular situations. This page has two parts.

(1) Grothendieck judges axiom At 14 ('peut-être facultative') somewhat ad hoc ('circonstanciel'). It is phrased in terms of sub-ateliers of a Fig(L), whereas it would more naturally be a stability condition. He prefers an optional variant, At 14 bis = 'At ens fac 5'.
- Hypotheses: X ∈ M and F' ≤ ∂X with F' ∈ M.
- Let F be the unique elementary figure of Fig(L) with ∂F = F'.
- Conclusion: F ∈ M.

In modern terms this is a 'filling', or cell-closure, axiom: every admissible sub-sphere of the boundary of an admissible cell bounds a unique elementary cell, and that cell is admissible. Uniqueness presumably comes from the linear/convex structure of Fig(L), where a cell is determined by its boundary, as for convex polytopes. He immediately notes that this fails for simplicial ateliers. Example: a 4-cycle of edges in the boundary of a tetrahedron bounds a quadrilateral, which is not a simplex. So the axiom holds for polyhedral/convex-cell structures but not for simplicial ones.

(2) He then turns to a sub-atelier F' ⊂ F, referring to conditions 'Sous at 1, 2', p. 47.
- Axioms At 1–7 (those not involving L) pass immediately to F'.
- For the axioms involving minimal elements (At 8, 9, 9_Σ, 10), one must first compare L, the minimal elements of F, with L', the minimal elements of F'.
- Trivially L ∩ F' ⊂ L': a figure minimal in F that lies in F' is minimal in F'.
- The next page asks for equality and introduces 'épaisse' and 'assez dense' sub-categories (Sous-cat 3, 3', 4) to secure it.
errors: No mathematical error. The claim that At 1–7 'se transportent aussitôt' to a sub-atelier is asserted without verification. It depends on the precise definitions of 'Sous at 1, 2', which are not on this page.
The uniqueness of an elementary figure with prescribed boundary is assumed for Fig(L); it is not justified here (presumably built into the definition of Fig(L)).

ideas.what: Optional 'filling' axiom At ens fac 5: an admissible sub-figure of the boundary of an admissible figure bounds a unique elementary figure, which is again admissible. Noted to fail for simplicial ateliers.
ideas.modern_name: Closure of a cell/polyhedral complex under filling boundary spheres (convex-polytopal vs simplicial complexes; regular CW posets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in combinatorial topology / polytope theory; no specific credit
ideas.where_published: Not in published texts. The tame-topology programme is only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the atelier axiomatics remains unpublished.

ideas.what: Passing atelier axioms to sub-ateliers; comparing the minimal elements L' of F' with L ∩ F' (L ∩ F' ⊂ L').
ideas.modern_name: Hereditary properties of sub-posets / subcomplexes; minimal elements of a sub-poset

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates a filling/stability axiom distinguishing polyhedral-cell ateliers from simplicial ones. This is part of an unpublished axiomatic 'atelier' framework for tame/combinatorial topology, and the page itself contains no completed result.
missed.quote: Considérons l'unique figure F ∈ Fig(L) qui soit élémentaire et telle que ∂F = F'. Alors F ∈ M. Mais ce n'est pas vrai pour les ateliers simpliciaux !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is marginal on its own. It documents how Grothendieck intended his 1986 Analysis situs axioms to separate convex-polyhedral from simplicial models, which is relevant to reconstructing his tame-topology programme. It is not a new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine axiom bookkeeping inside an unpublished axiomatic framework. The filling axiom and the sub-atelier remarks are elementary and have obvious analogues in combinatorial topology.
transcription_corrections: 'semble [-plus-] un peu observée seulement' is more likely 'semble [-plus-] un peu circonstancielle(ment)'.
'dans le nature' should read 'dans la nature'.
'En guise de cela' is uncertain; possibly 'D'autre part'.
The underlined heading 'At [-...-] 5' reads 'At ens fac 5' (At ens facultatif 5).
'il faut diriger premièrement ceci L et L'' is uncertain; likely 'il faut d'abord comparer/préciser L et L''.
